items.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: Benny Green and all those young guys I see coming out of here, it’s just amazing.

ctx.x: And if you can hear, see how you going to relate to what you haven’t heard or what you can’t hear? And music is relative if it’s nothing else. I mean otherwise, you’re just out there blowing and it doesn’t mean anything. It’s not going anywhere, it isn’t saying anything.

And the thing like this is a good thing, when young people can get to see us, talk to us, and we can get to hear them, and speak freely about certain things. I’ll tell you a funny thing that happened to me last night. The last two weeks or so, before I came on the boat, I’ve been Teaching Artist in Residence in the Manhattan School of Music. And it’s wonderful up there, these great young kids and things. And last night I was sitting at the table having dinner, and a beautiful little girl came up and says, “Mr.…
Yeah. It is nice to see that our tomorrows are really in very good hands.
